newsitem.title: USA: Showboat retains management of Sydney casino.
newsitem.headline: Showboat retains management of Sydney casino.

text.p: Showboat Inc said Saturday it will retain its rights to manage Sydney Harbour Casino and will remain the largest single shareholder of owner Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd.

Showboat issued the statement after it said it had been formally advised by Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd that the Australian company would not proceed with a proposed $A240 million deal with Showboat involving the Sydney casino.

Publishing and Broadcasting, in which the family of Australian billionaire Kerry Packer holds a 45 percent stake, had let lapse an agreement for it to buy 85 percent of the casino's management contract from Showboat.
The agreement also included an option by the Australian company to buy from Showboat a 10 percent stake that Showboat holds in the casino's owner.

Showboat, which owns casino-hotels here and in Atlantic City, N.J., said it holds a 24.6 percent stake in the Sydney casino company. Sydney Harbor Casino has been operating a temporary casino in Sydney since September 1995.
Showboat said that, in dropping the proposed deal, Publishing and Broadcasting had cited concerns unrelated to Showboat or to the Sydney casino.

In an announcement from Sydney on May 3, Publishing and Broadcasting said it had allowed the agreement deal to lapse because of difficulties encountered with the Casino Control Authority, the regulator of casinos in New South Wales.

"Now that PBL has chosen not to proceed, Showboat, Inc. will continue to work with the Board of Sydney Harbour Casino and the Showboat Australia management team to ensure the growth and prosperity of the casino so as to benefit both Showboat's and Sydney Harbour Casino's shareholders, customers and employees," said J. Kell Houssels, III, president and chief executive officer of Showboat.

Houssels noted that the litigation that challenged the casino license grant to Sydney Harbour Casino was concluded favorably and that construction of the permanent casino remains on budget and on schedule to open in December 1997.

"We look forward to retaining our existing position in the management company and in the ownership of Sydney Harbour Casino, which is expected to substantially increase the future earnings of our company," he said.
